records.title: Carrington Event
records.summary: The largest recorded geomagnetic storm. It disrupted telegraph systems worldwide and produced auroras near the equator.

records.title: Ground-level event of February 1956
records.summary: One of the most intense solar proton events detected by ground monitors.

records.title: August 1972 solar storm
records.summary: Occurred between Apollo 16 and Apollo 17. Analyses suggest an unshielded astronaut on the Moon could have received a dangerous dose, which shaped storm-shelter planning.

records.title: October 1989 events
records.summary: A series of large proton events, among the strongest of the space age.

records.title: Halloween storms
records.summary: Very large flares; ISS crew sheltered in the better-shielded Zvezda module, and Mars Odyssey's radiation instrument was damaged.

records.title: January 2005 ground-level event
records.summary: A fast event with particles arriving within about 15-30 minutes of the flare, showing how little warning crews may get.

records.title: September 2017 event at Mars
records.summary: Detected on the Mars surface by Curiosity's RAD instrument, which saw the surface dose roughly double, and by MAVEN in orbit.

records.title: May 2024 'Gannon' geomagnetic storm
records.summary: The strongest geomagnetic storm in two decades (G5), with auroras seen far from the poles.

records.title: Solar Cycle 25 maximum
records.summary: NASA and NOAA announced in October 2024 that the Sun had reached solar maximum, a period with more frequent flares and particle events.
